summary.text: James Clyburn is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 6th District, seeking re-election. A former teacher and South Carolina state official, he has represented the district since 1993 and has held House Democratic leadership posts including Majority Whip and Assistant Democratic Leader. He serves on the Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Sumter, South Carolina, in 1940. According to his official biography, he is the eldest son of a minister and a beautician.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from South Carolina State College in Orangeburg.

Began his career as a public-school teacher in Charleston and later worked as an employment counselor and as director of two youth and community development programs; Ballotpedia also lists work as a newspaper publisher.

Held South Carolina state posts including service on the State Employment Security Commission and State Commission for Farm Workers. Joined Gov. John C. West's (D) staff in 1971, which his official biography describes as making him the first African American advisor to a South Carolina governor.
Appointed South Carolina Human Affairs Commissioner by Gov. West in 1974 and served until 1992, when he left state government to run for Congress.

Took office in the U.S. House in 1993 and was elected co-president of his freshman class. He later served as Chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus and as Vice Chair and Chair of the House Democratic Caucus.

Served as House Majority Whip (2007 to 2010 and 2019 to 2022) and as Assistant Democratic Leader (2011 to 2018 and 2023 to March 2024); the Majority Whip is the third-ranking House leadership position. From 2019 to 2022 he also chaired the Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Crisis.
Serves on the House Appropriations Committee as Ranking Member of its Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and chairs the Democratic Faith Working Group.

According to his official biography, he sponsored legislation creating the Gullah/Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor, Congaree National Park and the Reconstruction Era National Historical Park, and authored the '10-20-30' federal funding formula. His awards include the NAACP's Spingarn Medal (2022) and the Presidential Medal of Freedom (2024).
His official biography says he met his late wife, Emily England Clyburn, in 1960; they had three daughters.
